One of Gideon's three hundred men, a young Israelite man with a short dark beard in a plain brown tunic and a tan headcloth, standing still in his place, holding a blazing torch high in his left hand and blowing a shofar: a long curved natural ram's horn, cream and light brown colored animal horn with a twisted shape, not metal, not a brass trumpet, held in his right hand, broken clay jar pieces at his feet, exactly two arms and exactly two hands.

Wide illustrated story panel for a children's Bible game, one single full-bleed scene with no border and no frame: night; on three low hills around a dark valley, three groups of Israelite men in plain brown and tan tunics and headcloths, stand still in their places, each man holding a blazing torch high in his left hand and blowing a shofar: a long curved natural ram's horn, cream and light brown colored animal horn with a twisted shape, not metal, not a brass trumpet, held in his right hand; broken pieces of clay jars lie at their feet; below in the valley the great Midianite camp of black tents is in confusion: tents shake and fall, and camels and people run away into the darkness; nobody is hit and nobody is hurt; nobody holds a sword. No crescent shapes, no moon ornaments, no religious symbols anywhere. Every person has exactly two arms, two hands, two legs and two feet.
